messages:
maria: Heads up - rollout for release-3.14 is paused. Observing a compile storm after the kernel-selector heuristic change in #3245, spiking p95/p99 and fill rate on the compile queue. deploy-bot: Deployment paused (release-3.14) by CI guard.
jon: ack. do we have a quick repro or CI artifacts?
priya: CI perf job 3.14-candidate failed with 3x compile tasks/sec sustained for ~6m. Attach logs: https://ci.internal/runs/8032
devon: quick summary from profiler: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.42 for short-seq workloads after the selector change. That forces different kernel paths and triggers many new compiles.
sam: re the selector change - it biases toward faster int8 kernels when batch_size >= 8. Seems fine, but cache key includes batch_shape and seq_len; we may be missing a normalization step.
ellie: if cache key expands with minor shape variants we blow up compile set. I see a bloom of unique keys in the last hour.
priya: logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] compile_queue.enqueue task_id=tx-9c4f kernel=int8_fused_256x128 seq=16 batch=8 model=resnet-like
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] compile_queue.enqueue task_id=tx-9c50 kernel=int8_fused_240x128 seq=15 batch=8 model=resnet-like
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] compile_worker.spawn compile=ok time_ms=2113
```
maria: that's the pattern. the selector produced two similar but distinct kernels (256 vs 240) for practically the same workload. compile storm follows.
jon: can we short-circuit by adding a cache normalization mapping: coerce kernel shapes to the nearest bucket? is there a cheap fix we can roll?
devon: quick patch idea: in selector, round ksize to step-of-16 for compilation key. I can prod a patch, but need to validate perf delta.
sam: +1. also add a defensive cap: if compile_queue.rate > 50/s, stop spawning new compiles and fall back to prev-compatible kernel for 1m. That would keep service up.
ellie: we should also check the autotune seed change from the merge - it added stochastic tie-breaker which can cause frequent kernel flips across nodes.
priya: bisect candidates: PR #3245 (selector), PR #3258 (autotune tie-breaker), merge commit c3f9b2a. CI points strongly at #3245 but tie-breaker amplifies.
maria: ops priority: 1) immediate hotfix to mute compile spawn (devon + sam), 2) revert candidate if hotfix causes regressions, 3) long-term selector normalization (jon + priya).
devon: cooking quick hotfix now. patch: ```diff
diff --git a/runtime/compile_manager.py b/runtime/compile_manager.py
@@
- if should_compile: spawn_compile(task)
+ if compile_spawn_rate() > 50: 
+     log.info('compile rate limit hit, falling back')
+     use_fallback_kernel(task)
+ else:
+     spawn_compile(task)
```
sam: will push to patch branch and run smoke.
buildbot: CI job compile-rate-mitigation started: https://ci.internal/job/compile-rate-mitigation/12
priya: while hotfix runs, I'll run a replay of short-seq traces to verify correctness of normalization candidate.
john: (typo: meant jon) seeing 503s creeping in? maria: yes, p99 latency climbed 2x for short-chat route. customers could be impacted, so keep this as rollout blocker until mitigated.
devon: hotfix pushed to canary pool. initial metrics: compile spawn rate down 8x, p99 back within 10% of baseline.
priya: normalization prototype: key = (model, round(seq_len/8)*8, bucket_batch(batch_size)) - reduces key cardinality by ~60% in replay.
jon: great. let's keep the hotfix for now and open a rollback PR for #3245 if normalization takes > 24h.
maria: decision: hold rollout, keep hotfix in canary, schedule rollback PR for selector change. devon/sam iterate on mitigation and post measured perf in #3245 thread.
sam: note for postmortem - autotune tie-breaker change should be gated behind a stability flag.
ellie: adding incident tag and creating a postmortem stub: https://wiki/internal/incidents/2026-03-18-compilestorm
priya: also capturing a short flamegraph excerpt for later: ```
flamegraph: compile_worker > compile_kernel > codegen > assembler > syscalls
peak time: 14:02:12 - 14:08:00
```
maria: thanks all. keep updates here. I'll sync with support to watch for customer noise. :eyes:
sam: +1, will follow up with PRs. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary patch (hotfix/compile-rate-mitigation) deployed to canary pool at 2026-03-18T14:12:03Z
buildbot: CI compile-rate-mitigation passed smoke, running regression suite.
jon: next steps: after stabilization, plan a targeted rollout with feature flags and telemetry for kernel-selection churn.
maria: timeline: 1h: confirm canary, 4h: rollback if any regression, 24h: ship normalized selector if tests green.
priya: filing links/artefacts here: traces: https://traces.internal/trace/abc123, ci: https://ci.internal/runs/8032, pr: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/3259
maria: closing the loop — keep logging verbose for selector keys for 6h. ping me if anything spikes again.
